source: KICD Environmental Activities, First Published in 2017; Revised 2024 (text layer)
status: outcomes from KICD's text, word for word; skills, prerequisites and misconceptions not yet mapped

learning_experiences: observe pictures and name materials used to clean different parts of the body,
draw and colour materials used to clean different parts of the body
match cleaning materials with pictures of body parts they are used to clean
watch a video clip or observe pictures on oral hygiene practises for personal well-being,
share information on problems related to oral hygiene,
practise brushing teeth for proper oral hygiene and personal well-being,
observe a demonstration on cleaning parts of the body,
follow appropriate steps to wash own face, hands, feet, and hair by careful use (no wastage) of cleaning agents and water,
sing a song or recite a poem on cleaning different parts of the body,
make and maintain a journal on cleaning different parts of the body for one week,
make a healthy habit poster showing the importance of oral habits.
key_inquiry_questions: How do you clean your body parts?
Why should we clean our body parts?
sub_strands.core_competences: Creativity and Imagination: learner exhibits the skill of originality when making a healthy habit poster showing the importance of oral habits.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: learner enhances diligence and excellence while cleaning body parts without wasting cleaning agents and water.
sub_strands.pcis:
Life Skills: learner develops self-awareness when taking care of different body parts.
Health Promotion Issues: learner develops the skill of cleaning own body parts as a way of practising personal cleanliness.
sub_strands.links: Taking an account of cleaning the body parts relates to the skill of journaling in English Language Activities.

outcomes.text: identify materials used to clean different parts of the body
wash face, teeth, hands, feet, and hair using locally available materials
appreciate the importance of a clean body for personal hygiene

learning_experiences: share ideas on different materials used to sweep, wipe, dust and collect litter at home,
draw and colour materials used to sweep, wipe, dust and collect litter at home,
share information on common accidents that occur at home,
select places at home or school where common accidents are likely to occur and share with peers,
practise appropriate pedestrian crossing,
manipulate digital devices to watch videos or observe pictures on ways of preventing accidents at home,
manipulate a digital device to watch a video, or observe pictures on ways of ensuring cleanliness in the home,
practise cleaning places and assorted items using different suitable cleaning materials at home or school.
key_inquiry_questions: How can you make your home environment clean and safe?
sub_strands.core_competences: Learning to Learn: learner develops independence when cleaning furniture using suitable materials.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: learner enhances self-drive when keeping the home environment clean such as practising cleaning assorted home items using suitable cleaning materials.
sub_strands.pcis: Disaster risk reduction: learner develops awareness of potential risk areas and objects that can cause harm/accidents to foster the safety of self and others.
sub_strands.links: Materials used for cleaning relate to items used in Creative Activities to clean self after finger painting activities.

outcomes.text: identify materials used to clean a home environment
state common accidents at home for personal and others’ safety
carry out activities to ensure cleanliness in the home
reflect on the importance of living in a clean home environment

learning_experiences: share information on different family needs,
manipulate a digital device to watch a video clip or observe pictures of different basic family needs,
draw and colour items that represent family needs,
observe pictures of food items used by family members,
match pictures of food items with their names,
recite poems or sing songs on different family needs,
manipulate digital devices when recording poems and songs on different family needs,
make picture cut-outs of food items and structures as basic needs in the family,
sort and group locally assorted food items into types of tastes,
create a one-week journal of healthy foods eaten,
make a nature corner with different food items found in the locality.
key_inquiry_questions: Which things do you use as a family at home?
How do you choose the food you eat?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Digital Literacy: learner manipulates digital devices when recording poems and songs on different family needs.
Self-efficacy: learner sorts and groups locally assorted food items into types of tastes.
sub_strands.values: Respect: learner appreciates diverse opinions when sharing information on different family needs.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills: learner develops the skill of self-awareness when drawing, colouring and grouping different family needs.
sub_strands.links: Basic needs of the family such as water relates to filling and emptying activities in Mathematical Activities.

outcomes.text: identify basic needs in the family
classify items and structures as basic needs in the family
categorise food from plants and animals eaten at home
select suitable food for a healthy body
appreciate different needs in the family

learning_experiences: manipulate a digital device to watch videos or observe pictures of the main physical features between home and school,
draw and colour the main physical features found between home and school,
interact with digital technology when playing educative games on locating main features between home and school,
role play safety measures to take on the way to school.
key_inquiry_questions: How do you identify your way to school?
How can you be safe while coming to school?
sub_strands.core_competences: Digital Literacy: learner interacts with digital technology when playing educative games to locate main features between home and school.
sub_strands.values: Unity: learner enriches cooperation and team spirit when role-playing safety measures to take on the way to school.
sub_strands.pcis: Safety: learner acquires child road safety awareness when role-playing safety measures to take on the way to school and back.
sub_strands.links: Drawing physical features between home and school relates to the skill of drawing and colouring in Creative Activities.

outcomes.text: identify the main physical features between home and school
draw main physical features between home and school
apply personal safety on the way to school
acknowledge the significance of identifying places using key features

learning_experiences: observe pictures or videos of people found in a market,
share information with peers on the roles of people found in a market,
use pictures or flashcards to pick out food items found in a local market,
draw and colour different food items found in a market,
use flashcards to sort and group food items into fruits and vegetables,
sort and group picture cut-outs of food items found in a market and make a portfolio.
recite poems and sing songs on food items found in the market.
sub_strands.core_competences: Communication and Collaboration: learner listens keenly and speaks effectively when sharing information with peers on the roles of people found in a market.
sub_strands.values: Unity: learner enhances cooperation with peers when drawing and colouring different food items found in the market.
sub_strands.pcis: Social-economic issues: learner develops the skill of career awareness when sharing information with peers on the roles of people found in a market.
sub_strands.links: Food items found in a market relate to concepts of sorting and grouping in Mathematical Activities.

outcomes.text: identify roles of people found in a market
list food items found in a market
categorise food items found in a market into fruits and vegetables
appreciate activities that are carried out in a market

learning_experiences: observe the sky during the day and at night and share observations with peers,
manipulate a digital device to watch video clips or observe pictures showing the appearance of the sky during the day and at night,
draw features appearing in the sky during the day and at night,
manipulate a digital device to watch video clips or observe pictures of different weather conditions,
draw symbols of different weather conditions in the locality,
observe prevailing weather conditions as an outdoor activity,
share ideas on prevailing weather conditions and make a simple weather chart,
tell age-appropriate stories about weather and weather conditions.
key_inquiry_questions: How does the sky appear at night and during the day?
sub_strands.core_competences: Communication: learner speaks engagingly when telling age-appropriate stories about weather and weather conditions
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: learner fosters commitment when making and maintaining a one-week daily journal on weather conditions.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills: learner develops time management skills when making and reading weather charts.
sub_strands.links: Appearance of the sky and conditions can be used when learning about creation in Religious Activities.

outcomes.text: describe the appearance of the sky during the day and at night
identify weather conditions in the locality
record different weather conditions in the locality
appreciate differences in weather conditions at different times of the day

learning_experiences: share ideas on ways of playing with soil for enjoyment,
share tasks when filling and emptying cans with soil in turns,
make different patterns using soil as paint,
manipulate a digital device to watch videos or observe pictures of objects made from soil,
model different objects using soil,
sing relevant songs to peers while playing with soil for fun.
clean or tidy up the working space after modelling activities and wash hands with soap and clean running water.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is playing with soil important to us?
sub_strands.core_competences: Self-efficacy: learner develops high self-esteem when modelling different objects using soil.
sub_strands.values: Social Justice: learner enhances cooperation when filling and emptying cans with soil in turns.
sub_strands.pcis: Health Promotion Issues: learner develops the skill of washing hands with soap and clean running water after playing with soil.
sub_strands.links: Aspects of soil relate to modelling items using soil in Creative Activities.

outcomes.text: identify ways of playing with soil for enjoyment
play with soil for enjoyment
model objects using soil at school
develop curiosity in playing with soil for enjoyment

learning_experiences: take a sound walk in the immediate environment to identify sounds from humans, animals, machines and natural sources and share with peers,
manipulate digital devices to watch a video clip on ways of creating sound using the body, objects and voice,
listen to an audio clip on ways of creating sound using the body, objects and voice,
imitate and record videos or audio sounds from people, animals, machines and natural sources,
use video clips or audio files to listen to various sounds that alert people to danger,
role play sounds that alert people to danger,
role play on appropriate responses to vehicle sounds (horn sounds, bells, sirens) to keep safe in the environment,
explore sources of loud sounds in the immediate environment,
talk about what happens to a person when near loud sounds,
observe pictures or videos that show how to protect oneself from loud sounds,
practise obeying sounds that alert us to danger for appropriate response.
key_inquiry_questions: How do animals and other objects in our environment produce sounds?
Why are sounds important in our lives?
sub_strands.core_competences: Self-efficacy: learner develops confidence when imitating various sounds produced by animals or objects.
sub_strands.values: Patriotism: learner enhances loyalty when obeying sounds that alert on danger for appropriate response.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills: learner uses common courteous words when engaging with peers to role-play sounds that alert on danger.
sub_strands.links: Sounds in the immediate environment draw concepts in Creative Activities.

outcomes.text: identify sounds in the immediate environment
create sounds from objects for enjoyment
discriminate sounds that alert on danger for an appropriate response
acknowledge sounds that alert us to dangers

learning_experiences: manipulate digital devices to watch videos or observe pictures of different sources of water,
develop originality skills when drawing and colouring different sources of water,
complete a simple word puzzle on sources of water at home and school,
collaboratively model sources of water in class learning spaces or corners using locally available materials,
observe and write uses of water at home and school,
share experiences with peers on the careful use of water in the home and school,
role play water conservation activities that can be used at home and school,
make a poster on water conservation (reducing the use of water) at home and school.
key_inquiry_questions: How can you use water without wasting it?
Why do we care for water sources?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to Learn: learner models water sources in the class learning space or corner using locally available materials.
Creativity and Imagination: learner develops originality skills when drawing and colouring different sources of water.
sub_strands.values: Unity: learner collaboratively models sources of water in class learning spaces or corners using locally available materials.
sub_strands.pcis: Health promotion issues: learner drinks clean water and role-plays using water sparingly for personal wellbeing.
sub_strands.links: Making a poster on water conservation at home and school draws knowledge from writing skills in English Language Activities.

outcomes.text: identify sources of water in the immediate environment
record uses of water at home and school
conserve water at home and school
acknowledge different sources of water in the immediate environment

learning_experiences: take a nature walk to explore parts of plants,
manipulate a digital device to watch video clips or observe pictures and photographs to identify different parts of a plant,
observe safety during collecting and observing young plants in the locality,
indicate parts of a plant (flower, leaves, stem, roots) using real plants or pictures,
colour parts of a plant and display own work for further learning and peer assessment,
plant seeds in the nature corner of the class, in a school garden or flowerbed,
practise watering plants found in the immediate environment.
key_inquiry_questions: How can you care for plants in your environment?
sub_strands.core_competences: Learning to Learn: learner develops concepts of plants when going for a nature walk to explore different parts of plants in the immediate environment.
sub_strands.values: Patriotism: learner enriches citizenship when showing love to the country by watering plants found in the immediate environment.
sub_strands.pcis: Environmental education and climate change: learner observes safety and responsibility when collecting young plants in the locality.
sub_strands.links: Plants relate to the concept of creation in Religious Activities.

outcomes.text: identify parts of a plant found in the school garden or compound
draw different parts of a plant found at school
carry out activities that conserve plants in the immediate environment
advocate for the conservation of plants in the immediate environment

learning_experiences: manipulate a digital device to watch or observe pictures of domestic animals,
take a nature walk in the immediate environment to observe and write the names of domestic animals,
draw and colour domestic animals used as food in the locality.
manipulate a digital device to watch video clips of domestic animals being watered, fed and treated,
share with peers on safety precautions taken when feeding and watering domestic animals,
water and feed some domestic animals in the immediate environment accompanied by a caregiver,
wash hands using clean running water after interacting with animals for personal hygiene,
make a journal on basic care activities done to domestic animals at home or school,
listen to stories on animals for enjoyment,
gather more information on care for domestic animals from parents or guardians and write them clearly and correctly.
key_inquiry_questions: How can you care for animals in your immediate environment?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to Learn: learner develops exploration skills when taking a nature walk to observe and write the names of domestic animals.
Communication and Collaboration: learner writes clearly and correctly when gathering more information on care for domestic animals from parents or guardians.
sub_strands.values:
Love: learner enhances compassion when portraying a caring attitude during the watering and feeding of some domestic animals in the immediate environment.
Unity: learner enriches cooperation when displaying team spirit during nature walks to observe domestic animals.
sub_strands.pcis:
Health promotion issues: learner develops hand washing skills using clean running water after feeding and watering animals.
Life Skills: learner develops empathy and takes precautions while feeding/watering domestic animals.
sub_strands.links: Listening to stories on animals for enjoyment relates to active listening in English Language Activities.

outcomes.text: identify domestic animals in the immediate environment
list domestic animals used as food in the locality
carry out basic care activities for small domestic animals
acknowledge the diversity of animals in the immediate environment

indicators.indicator: Ability to practise proper hygiene using locally available materials. Ability to practise good healthy habits at home and school. Ability to identify safety precautions at home and school.

levels.EE: Practises proper hygiene using locally available materials most frequently. Practises good healthy habits at home and school most frequently. Identifies safety precautions at home and school with in-depth details.
levels.ME: Practises proper hygiene using locally available materials. Practises good healthy habits at home and school. Identifies safety precautions at home and school.
levels.AE: Practises proper hygiene using locally available materials occasionally. Practises good healthy habits at home and school occasionally. Identifies safety precautions at home and school with minimal details.
levels.BE: Rarely practises proper hygiene using locally available materials. Rarely practises good healthy habits at home and school. Identifies safety precautions at home and school without details.

indicators.indicator: Ability to observe safety precautions in the immediate environment. Ability to identify ways of playing with soil and sounds. Ability to record weather conditions in the locality.

levels.EE: Observes safety precautions in the immediate environment most keenly. Identifies ways of playing with soil and sounds with in-depth details. Records weather conditions in the locality most precisely.
levels.ME: Observes safety precautions in the immediate environment keenly. Identifies ways of playing with soil and sounds. Records weather conditions in the locality precisely.
levels.AE: Observes safety precautions in the immediate environment less keenly. Identifies ways of playing with soil and sounds with minimal details. Records weather conditions in the locality less precisely.
levels.BE: Observes safety precautions in the immediate environment with prompts. Identifies a way of playing with soil and sounds without details. Records weather conditions in the locality imprecisely.

indicators.indicator: Ability to record the uses of water at home and school. Ability to conserve water and plants in the immediate environment. Ability to care for domestic animals in the immediate environment. Suggested Resources, Assessment Methods and Non-Formal Activities Suggested Learning Resources Suggested Assessment Methods ● Approved curriculum support materials ● Resources from the local environment (home and school) ● Stationery ● Digital devices ● Manilla Papers ● Drawing materials ● Clay soil ● Water ● Plastic bottles ● Pictures or picture cut-outs /Newspaper cuttings/Photographs ● Flashcards ● Charts Non-formal Activities that support learning ● Games and sports ● Clubs and societies ● Other school events

levels.EE: Records the uses of water at home and school most precisely. Very often takes utmost care to conserve water and plants in the immediate environment. Cares for domestic animals in the immediate environment most frequently.
levels.ME: Records the uses of water at home and school. Conserves water and plants in the immediate environment. Cares for domestic animals in the immediate environment.
levels.AE: Records the uses of water at home and school less precisely. Sometimes conserves water and plants in the immediate environment. Cares for domestic animals in the immediate environment occasionally. ● Observation ● Aural questions ● Oral question ● Written tests ● Self-assessment ● Peer assessment ● Projects
levels.BE: Records the uses of water at home and school imprecisely. Rarely conserves water and plants in the immediate environment. Rarely cares for domestic animals in the immediate environment.
